descriptionChirho: A Babylonian official present at the fall of Jerusalem (Jeremiah 39), whose compound Akkadian name means 'Nergal, protect the king.' The four clusters represent components of this multi-part proper name that were over-split by tokenization: 'Nergal' (the deity element), 'sar/prince-of' (the title element), 'Etser' (the protection element), and the full compound with conjunction. Arabic Nirjalu-ra'isu-Asara, Spanish Nergal-Sar-Etser, Hindi Nergal-hakim-Eser, Korean Nereugal-Saresum, Swahili Nergali-Saretseri all confirm these are parts of one name.
